title: GD 69 durian (Galang Durian 69): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: GD 69 durian: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: GD 69 durian is a durian variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: GD 69 is a registered durian variety, also sold or known as Galang Durian 69 or Galang Durian. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Dr 02. Angel Galang bred it. Its record notes a yield of 50 fruits.

blocks.caption: Key facts of GD 69
rows: Galang Durian 69, Galang Durian, NSIC Dr 02

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of GD 69 was about 10 years old and about 8 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 50 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in August October. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit durian fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of GD 69 weighs about 3720 grams, and its shape is obovate. The flesh is yellow orange and firm. Its sweetness measured 19.2 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 44.8 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is August October, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** About 3.7 kg, yellow green, firm yellow orange flesh, sweet and melting, 19.2 Brix, about 45 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the registry's highest edible share among durians (about 45 percent), from a Calinan farm. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant GD 69 durian

Davao growers plant named clones such as Puyat and Arancillo for their thick, creamy flesh and small seeds. Plant grafted trees of a known clone, and mix clones for better fruit set. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Galang Durian 69 the same as GD 69?
items.a: Yes. Galang Durian 69 is another name for GD 69, registered as NSIC 1995 Dr 02. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 50 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of GD 69?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
